# CAL KERNELS (test)

Five machines of synthetic SHARC+ kernels with known instruction counts per render call (alu 20,050, dm 19,959, mem 19,244, branch 20,046, mix 19,956), for the calibration profile `kernels` (`devices/calibration/profiles/kernels.toml`): factors of a device and of the emulator are fitted per kind of instruction. The mix of each kernel and the memory it touches are in the header of `src/dsp/cal_kernels.s`. The machines have no parameter and render silence (mix: a signal below 1e-6); a voice never ends, so one press gives exactly one call per block, and the profile puts a module-free case between kernel cases (the restart ends the voice). A case names a machine as `test/cal-kernels#n` (n counts from 1 in the order of `[[machine]]`). `tests/kernels.rig.test.ts` pins the counts per device; the conformance suite runs the first machine (alu) against the share of the headroom that its one declared voice may use.

Emulator check (DN2, profile `kernels`): the machine row averages the rig count plus the 14 instructions of the adapter wrapper for every kernel (alu 20,064, dm 19,973, mem 19,258, branch 20,060, mix 19,970), 0.95 to 1.0 calls per block, and a block never holds two calls. An earlier build with a voice-life counter and retriggers showed mem about 18 below the rig count; with one voice per case that difference is gone.

Budget: each machine declares one voice, so conformance gives it the share `headroom / voices` of the device (the broker's rule `max(costs) x voices`), not the 1/16 share.
